newsitem.title: GERMANY: German pensions to rise by 1.65 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: German pensions to rise by 1.65 pct in July.

text.p: German state pensions will rise by 1.65 percent from July 1 in the west of the country and by 5.55 percent in the formerly communist east, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet decided on Wednesday.
The decision, which must be approved by the Bundesrat upper house of parliament, would increase average pensions in eastern Germany to 85.2 percent of the western level from 82.3 percent.
The so-called standard pension, which is based on a working life of 45 years for an average wage, would rise to 1,975 marks from 1,942 marks, officials said.

The parliamentary parties in the Kohl coalition on Tuesday approved a plan to introduce a pensions reform in 1999 which would cut old age pay to 64 percent of average net wages by 2030 from 70 percent now.
The plan would allow a one-point cut in contributions from current record levels of 20.3 percent by raising indirect taxes to cover some non-welfare items currently borne by the state pensions fund.
